answers.label: Q.1
answers.solution:
Take away the remainders. The required number divides each of these exactly:
\(398 - 7 = 391\), \(436 - 11 = 425\), \(542 - 15 = 527\).

So the largest such number is the HCF of 391, 425 and 527.
\(391 = 17 \times 23\)
\(425 = 17 \times 25 = 5^2 \times 17\)
\(527 = 17 \times 31\)

The only common factor is 17, so HCF = 17.

Check: 17 is larger than every remainder (7, 11, 15), so these remainders are possible.

So, the largest number is 17.

answers.label: Q.2
answers.solution:
First find each square root.
\(\sqrt{1204.09} = \sqrt{\frac{120409}{100}} = \frac{347}{10} = 34.7\) (since \(347^2 = 120409\))
\(\sqrt{125.44} = \sqrt{\frac{12544}{100}} = \frac{112}{10} = 11.2\) (since \(112^2 = 12544\))

Now substitute:
\(\frac{34.7 - 11.2}{34.7 + 11.2} = \frac{23.5}{45.9} = \frac{235}{459}\)

\(235 = 5 \times 47\) and \(459 = 3^3 \times 17\) have no common factor, so the fraction is in its lowest terms.

So, the answer is \(\frac{235}{459}\) (about 0.512).

answers.label: Q.3
answers.solution:
Perimeter of a rectangle \(= 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{breadth})\).

Add the two sides, collecting like terms:
\((-6p^3 + 7p^2q^2 + pq) + (-5p^3 + 9p^2q^2 + 7pq)\)
\(= (-6 - 5)p^3 + (7 + 9)p^2q^2 + (1 + 7)pq\)
\(= -11p^3 + 16p^2q^2 + 8pq\)

Multiply by 2:
\(2(-11p^3 + 16p^2q^2 + 8pq) = -22p^3 + 32p^2q^2 + 16pq\)

So, the perimeter is \(-22p^3 + 32p^2q^2 + 16pq\).

answers.label: Q.5
answers.finalAnswer: Interior angle of a regular pentagon = 108° = 3 × 36° (exterior angle of a regular decagon)
answers.solution:
The printed question says "a regular polygon" without naming it; the statement is true for a regular pentagon, which is the polygon meant.

Exterior angle of a regular decagon (10 sides):
\(\frac{360^\circ}{10} = 36^\circ\)

Three times this is \(3 \times 36^\circ = 108^\circ\).

Exterior angle of a regular pentagon (5 sides) \(= \frac{360^\circ}{5} = 72^\circ\), so its interior angle \(= 180^\circ - 72^\circ = 108^\circ\).

So the interior angle of a regular pentagon \(= 108^\circ = 3 \times 36^\circ\), three times the exterior angle of a regular decagon. Hence proved.

answers.label: Q.6
answers.solution:
Let the old price be Rs 100 per kg and the old consumption 1 kg, so the expenditure is Rs 100.

New price \(= 100 + 20\% \text{ of } 100 = \text{Rs } 120\) per kg.

To keep spending Rs 100, the new consumption \(= \frac{100}{120} = \frac{5}{6}\) kg.

Reduction \(= 1 - \frac{5}{6} = \frac{1}{6}\) kg.

Percent reduction \(= \frac{1}{6} \times 100\% = 16\frac{2}{3}\%\).

(Shortcut: \(\frac{20}{100 + 20} \times 100\% = 16\frac{2}{3}\%\).)

So, Dinesh should reduce his consumption by \(16\frac{2}{3}\%\).

answers.label: Q.7
answers.solution:
Let the HCF be \(h\). Then the LCM is \(9h\).

HCF + LCM = 500:
\(h + 9h = 500\)
\(10h = 500\)
\(h = 50\)

(Then LCM = 450, and 450 is a multiple of 50, as it must be.)

So, the HCF is 50.

answers.label: Q.8
answers.solution:
Cross-multiply:
\((x + 1)^2 (x + 4) = (x + 2)^2 (x + 2) = (x + 2)^3\)

Left side:
\((x^2 + 2x + 1)(x + 4) = x^3 + 4x^2 + 2x^2 + 8x + x + 4 = x^3 + 6x^2 + 9x + 4\)

Right side:
\((x + 2)^3 = x^3 + 6x^2 + 12x + 8\)

Equate them and cancel \(x^3 + 6x^2\):
\(9x + 4 = 12x + 8\)
\(-3x = 4\)
\(x = -\frac{4}{3}\)

Check: \(x + 2 = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(x + 4 = \frac{8}{3}\) are not zero, so the value is allowed.

So, \(x = -\frac{4}{3}\).

answers.label: Q.9
answers.solution:
Let the man have Rs \(x\) at first.

After losing 20%, he has \(80\%\) of \(x = \frac{4}{5}x\).

He spends 25% of this, so he keeps 75% of it:
\(\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{4}{5}x = \frac{3}{5}x\)

This is Rs 480:
\(\frac{3}{5}x = 480\)
\(x = 480 \times \frac{5}{3} = 800\)

So, he originally had Rs 800.

answers.label: Q.11
answers.solution:
Let the speed of the faster car be \(x\) km/h. Then the slower car's speed is \((x - 10)\) km/h.

The cars move towards each other, so together they close the gap at \(x + (x - 10) = (2x - 10)\) km/h.

After 6 hours they are still 30 km apart (they have not yet met), so together they have covered
\(690 - 30 = 660\) km.

\(6(2x - 10) = 660\)
\(2x - 10 = 110\)
\(2x = 120\)
\(x = 60\)

Slower car: \(60 - 10 = 50\) km/h.

Check: in 6 hours, \(6 \times 60 + 6 \times 50 = 360 + 300 = 660\) km, leaving \(690 - 660 = 30\) km.

(If instead the cars had already crossed and were 30 km apart, they would have covered 720 km, giving 65 km/h and 55 km/h; the usual reading is that they have not yet met.)

So, the speeds are 60 km/h and 50 km/h.

answers.solution:
Volume of brass \(= 2.2\) cubic dm. Since 1 dm = 10 cm, 1 cubic dm \(= 1000\) cubic cm.
Volume \(= 2.2 \times 1000 = 2200 \text{ cm}^3\)

Diameter of wire = 0.50 cm, so radius \(r = 0.25 = \frac{1}{4}\) cm.

The wire is a cylinder of length \(h\):
\(\pi r^2 h = 2200\)
\(\frac{22}{7} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{4} \times h = 2200\)
\(\frac{22}{112} h = 2200\)
\(h = 2200 \times \frac{112}{22} = 100 \times 112 = 11200\) cm

\(11200\) cm \(= 112\) m.

So, the length of the wire is 112 m.

answers.label: Q.13
answers.solution:
Let the three consecutive numbers be \(x\), \(x + 1\) and \(x + 2\).

\(x + (x + 1) + (x + 2) = 156\)
\(3x + 3 = 156\)
\(3x = 153\)
\(x = 51\)

The numbers are 51, 52 and 53.

\(52 = 13 \times 4\), while 51 and 53 are not multiples of 13.

So, the number which is a multiple of 13 is 52.

answers.label: Q.14
answers.solution:
The printed question has a "+" sign, but \(\sqrt[3]{968} + \sqrt[3]{1375}\) does not simplify to a number without a calculator. The numbers are chosen so that their PRODUCT is a perfect cube, so the question is read as \(\sqrt[3]{968} \times \sqrt[3]{1375}\).

Prime factors:
\(968 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 11 \times 11 = 2^3 \times 11^2\)
\(1375 = 5 \times 5 \times 5 \times 11 = 5^3 \times 11\)

\(\sqrt[3]{968} \times \sqrt[3]{1375} = \sqrt[3]{2^3 \times 11^2 \times 5^3 \times 11}\)
\(= \sqrt[3]{2^3 \times 5^3 \times 11^3}\)
\(= 2 \times 5 \times 11 = 110\)

So, the answer is 110.

(Taken exactly as printed, with "+": \(\sqrt[3]{968} = 2\sqrt[3]{121}\) and \(\sqrt[3]{1375} = 5\sqrt[3]{11}\), so the sum is \(2\sqrt[3]{121} + 5\sqrt[3]{11}\), about 21.01, which cannot be simplified further.)

answers.solution:
Let the number be \(x\).

\(\frac{3}{5}x - \frac{2}{7}x = 44\)

LCM of 5 and 7 is 35:
\(\frac{21x - 10x}{35} = 44\)
\(\frac{11x}{35} = 44\)
\(x = 44 \times \frac{35}{11} = 4 \times 35 = 140\)

Check: \(\frac{3}{5} \times 140 = 84\), \(\frac{2}{7} \times 140 = 40\), and \(84 - 40 = 44\).

So, the number is 140.

answers.finalAnswer: 100 tickets of Rs 2.50; 200 tickets of Rs 5
answers.solution:
Let the number of Rs 2.50 tickets be \(x\). Then the number of Rs 5 tickets is \(300 - x\).

Total sale:
\(2.5x + 5(300 - x) = 1250\)
\(2.5x + 1500 - 5x = 1250\)
\(-2.5x = -250\)
\(x = 100\)

Rs 5 tickets: \(300 - 100 = 200\).

Check: \(100 \times 2.50 + 200 \times 5 = 250 + 1000 = 1250\).

So, 100 tickets of Rs 2.50 and 200 tickets of Rs 5 were sold.

answers.label: Q.18
answers.solution:
When a die is tossed once, the possible outcomes are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Total outcomes = 6.

(a) Even prime numbers among them: only 2. Favourable outcomes = 1.
\(P(\text{even prime}) = \frac{1}{6}\)

(b) A number that is neither prime nor composite: only 1 (the primes are 2, 3, 5 and the composites are 4, 6). Favourable outcomes = 1.
\(P(\text{neither prime nor composite}) = \frac{1}{6}\)

So, the outcomes are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; (a) \(\frac{1}{6}\); (b) \(\frac{1}{6}\).

answers.solution:
The strip is \(1\frac{1}{4}\) cm wide, exactly one circle's diameter, so the circles are cut in a single row along the length.

Number of circles \(= 8\frac{3}{4} \div 1\frac{1}{4} = \frac{35}{4} \div \frac{5}{4} = \frac{35}{5} = 7\)

Area of the strip \(= \frac{35}{4} \times \frac{5}{4} = \frac{175}{16} \text{ cm}^2\)

Radius of each circle \(= \frac{5}{8}\) cm.
Area of one circle \(= \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{5}{8} \times \frac{5}{8} = \frac{550}{448} = \frac{275}{224} \text{ cm}^2\)

Area of 7 circles \(= 7 \times \frac{275}{224} = \frac{275}{32} \text{ cm}^2\)

Wastage \(= \frac{175}{16} - \frac{275}{32} = \frac{350 - 275}{32} = \frac{75}{32} \text{ cm}^2 = 2\frac{11}{32} \text{ cm}^2\) (about 2.34 cm²).

So, Shalini can cut 7 full circles, and the wastage is \(\frac{75}{32}\) cm² \(= 2\frac{11}{32}\) cm².

In the figure, PQRS is a rectangle and its diagonals PR and QS meet at O.

The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so \(OP = OQ\).

In \(\triangle OPQ\), \(OP = OQ\), so the angles opposite them are equal:

answers.solution:
Take the number of toffees bought of each kind as the LCM of 9 and 11, which is 99.

Cost of 99 toffees at 9 for Rs 10 \(= \frac{10}{9} \times 99 = \text{Rs } 110\)
Cost of 99 toffees at 11 for Rs 10 \(= \frac{10}{11} \times 99 = \text{Rs } 90\)

Total toffees = 198. Total cost price \(= 110 + 90 = \text{Rs } 200\).

Selling at 10 for Rs 10 means Re 1 each.
Selling price of 198 toffees = Rs 198.

Since SP < CP, there is a loss.
Loss \(= 200 - 198 = \text{Rs } 2\)

Loss percent \(= \frac{2}{200} \times 100\% = 1\%\)

So, there is a loss of 1%.

answers.label: Q.22
answers.solution:
Work in centimetres.
Length of pencil \(h = 10\) cm.
Radius of pencil \(= \frac{7}{2}\) mm \(= 0.35\) cm.
Radius of graphite \(= \frac{1}{2}\) mm \(= 0.05\) cm.

Volume of graphite:
\(\pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times 0.05 \times 0.05 \times 10 = \frac{22}{7} \times 0.025 = \frac{0.55}{7} \text{ cm}^3\)

Volume of wood = volume of whole pencil minus volume of graphite:
\(\frac{22}{7} \times (0.35^2 - 0.05^2) \times 10 = \frac{22}{7} \times (0.1225 - 0.0025) \times 10 = \frac{22}{7} \times 1.2 = \frac{26.4}{7} \text{ cm}^3\)

Weight = volume \(\times\) specific gravity (density).
Weight of wood \(= \frac{26.4}{7} \times 0.7 = 2.64\) g
Weight of graphite \(= \frac{0.55}{7} \times 2.1 = 0.55 \times 0.3 = 0.165\) g

Total weight \(= 2.64 + 0.165 = 2.805\) g

So, the weight of the whole pencil is 2.805 g.

answers.solution:
Let the sum be Rs \(P\). Rate = 10% per annum, time = 2 years.

Simple interest \(= \frac{P \times 10 \times 2}{100} = \frac{P}{5}\)

Amount at compound interest \(= P\left(1 + \frac{10}{100}\right)^2 = P \times \frac{121}{100}\)
Compound interest \(= \frac{121P}{100} - P = \frac{21P}{100}\)

Difference:
\(\frac{21P}{100} - \frac{20P}{100} = \frac{P}{100}\)

\(\frac{P}{100} = 500\)
\(P = 50000\)

Check: SI = Rs 10,000, CI = Rs 10,500, difference = Rs 500.

So, the sum is Rs 50,000.

answers.label: Q.24
answers.solution:
The food was enough for 120 men for 200 days.

After 5 days, the food left is enough for 120 men for \(200 - 5 = 195\) days.

Now 30 men die, so the men left \(= 120 - 30 = 90\).

Fewer men make the food last longer (inverse proportion):
\(120 \times 195 = 90 \times d\)
\(d = \frac{120 \times 195}{90} = \frac{4 \times 195}{3} = 4 \times 65 = 260\)

So, the remaining food will last 260 days.

Money available = Rs 20,000.

At the old price of Rs 800, he could buy \(\frac{20000}{800} = 25\) bicycles.

New price \(= 800 + 25\% \text{ of } 800 = 800 + \frac{25}{100} \times 800 = 800 + 200 = \text{Rs } 1000\)

Number of bicycles at the new price \(= \frac{20000}{1000} = 20\)

So, he can purchase 20 bicycles (5 fewer than before).

answers.label: Q.27
answers.finalAnswer: Trapezium PQRS with PQ = 8 cm, ∠Q = 60°, QR = 6 cm, RS = 4 cm drawn parallel to PQ; PS measures about 5.3 cm
answers.solution:
Rough figure: draw a trapezium with PQ at the bottom, R and S at the top, and SR parallel to PQ.

Steps of construction:
1. Draw the line segment \(PQ = 8\) cm.
2. At Q, construct \(\angle PQX = 60^\circ\) with ruler and compass (draw an arc with centre Q cutting QP, then from that point cut an equal arc on it; join Q to the cut point).
3. With centre Q and radius 6 cm, cut QX at R. So \(QR = 6\) cm.
4. At R, draw a ray RY parallel to PQ, on the same side as P. (Construct \(\angle QRY = 120^\circ\), since co-interior angles \(\angle Q + \angle R = 180^\circ\); or copy \(\angle XQP\) at R as corresponding angles.)
5. With centre R and radius 4 cm, cut RY at S. So \(RS = 4\) cm.
6. Join PS.

PQRS is the required trapezium, with \(PQ \parallel RS\).

Measurements to check:
- \(\angle R = 120^\circ\).
- Height of the trapezium (distance between PQ and RS) \(= 6 \times \sin 60^\circ \approx 5.2\) cm.
- \(PS \approx 5.3\) cm and \(\angle P \approx 79^\circ\), \(\angle S \approx 101^\circ\).

So, the trapezium PQRS is constructed with PQ = 8 cm, QR = 6 cm, RS = 4 cm, \(\angle Q = 60^\circ\) and PQ parallel to RS.

answers.label: Q.28
answers.solution:
In the figure: \(\angle 1 = \angle PST\), \(\angle 2 = \angle TSR\), \(\angle 3 = \angle STP\), \(\angle 4 = \angle RTQ\), \(\angle 5 = \angle TRQ\), \(\angle 6 = \angle SRT\), \(\angle 7 = \angle STR\).

Given: PQRS is a parallelogram, T is the midpoint of PQ, and ST bisects \(\angle S\), so \(\angle 1 = \angle 2\).

(a) To prove QR = QT.
\(SR \parallel PQ\) and ST is a transversal, so \(\angle 2 = \angle 3\) (alternate angles).
Since \(\angle 1 = \angle 2\), we get \(\angle 1 = \angle 3\).
In \(\triangle PST\), sides opposite equal angles are equal, so \(PT = PS\).
But \(PS = QR\) (opposite sides of a parallelogram) and \(PT = QT\) (T is the midpoint of PQ).
Therefore \(QR = QT\).

(b) To prove RT bisects \(\angle R\).
In \(\triangle QTR\), \(QT = QR\), so the angles opposite them are equal: \(\angle 4 = \angle 5\).
\(SR \parallel PQ\) and RT is a transversal, so \(\angle 6 = \angle 4\) (alternate angles).
Therefore \(\angle 5 = \angle 6\), so RT bisects \(\angle R\).

(c) To prove \(\angle STR = 90^\circ\).
\(SP \parallel RQ\), so \(\angle S + \angle R = 180^\circ\) (co-interior angles of a parallelogram).
Since ST bisects \(\angle S\) and RT bisects \(\angle R\):
\(\angle 2 + \angle 6 = \frac{1}{2}\angle S + \frac{1}{2}\angle R = \frac{1}{2} \times 180^\circ = 90^\circ\)
In \(\triangle STR\), \(\angle 7 = 180^\circ - (\angle 2 + \angle 6) = 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ\).

So, QR = QT, RT bisects \(\angle R\), and \(\angle STR = 90^\circ\). Hence proved.

answers.label: Q.29
answers.solution:
Every stack must have the same height (the same number of books), and each stack holds books of one subject only. To have the fewest stacks, each stack should hold as many books as possible, so we need the HCF of 336, 240 and 96.

\(336 = 2^4 \times 3 \times 7\)
\(240 = 2^4 \times 3 \times 5\)
\(96 = 2^5 \times 3\)

HCF \(= 2^4 \times 3 = 48\). So each stack has 48 books.

English stacks \(= \frac{336}{48} = 7\)
Mathematics stacks \(= \frac{240}{48} = 5\)
Science stacks \(= \frac{96}{48} = 2\)

Total stacks \(= 7 + 5 + 2 = 14\)

So, there will be 14 stacks (of 48 books each).

answers.label: Q.30
answers.solution:
When two dice are thrown, each die has 6 outcomes, so the total number of outcomes \(= 6 \times 6 = 36\).

Outcomes with a sum of 5:
(1, 4), (2, 3), (3, 2), (4, 1)
Number of favourable outcomes = 4.

\(P(\text{sum} = 5) = \frac{4}{36} = \frac{1}{9}\)

So, the probability of getting a sum of 5 is \(\frac{1}{9}\).
